name: Adlai
title: Father of Shaphat, who had charge of David's cattle
summary: Adlai is known from 1 Chronicles 27:29, where he is identified as the father of Shaphat. Shaphat was the administrator who had charge of the cattle in the valleys under King David’s administration. Adlai is mentioned only this one time in the biblical writings, but the context places him among the circle of the king’s trusted officials. The fact that his son was given such an administrative role suggests that the family held a certain standing and position in the united kingdom. Adlai’s mention is an example of how Chronicles systematically records genealogies connected to the administration of the realm, thereby preserving names that otherwise would have been lost to later generations.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the list of David's officials
keyEvents.description: Adlai is mentioned as the father of Shaphat, who was responsible for the cattle in the valleys during King David's administration. This is the only biblical reference to Adlai.

keyEvents.title: David's organization of the kingdom's resources
keyEvents.description: King David organized his kingdom with various officials who were responsible for different areas, including grain stores, vineyards, olive groves, and livestock. Shaphat, son of Adlai, was among these trusted servants, specifically in charge of the cattle in the valleys.

versions.summary: Adlai is a biblical figure mentioned only once in 1 Chronicles 27:29. He was the father of Shaphat, who had responsibility for the cattle grazing in the valleys during King David's reign. Adlai is thus known as the father of one of David's trusted servants.
versions.title: Father of Shaphat, overseer of David's shepherds
versions.reason: [major] Adlai is not described as a 'leader' in the Bible. He is mentioned only as the father of Shaphat. It is Shaphat who holds a leadership role, not Adlai himself. The role should be changed to 'father' to reflect the only thing we know about him.; [minor] Four key events are excessive for someone mentioned in just one verse. The events overlap significantly. It is recommended to reduce them to two events to avoid redundancy.; [minor] Footnotes are missing. A person mentioned only once deserves at least a linguistic footnote on the meaning of the name and a historical note about David's administrative system.; [minor] The Shaphat ID 'sjafat' should be verified. There are several people named Shaphat in the Bible (including the father of the prophet Elisha). It is important that the correct Shaphat is referenced, for example 'shaphat-adlai' if disambiguation is needed.

versions.summary: Adlai is a biblical figure mentioned only once in 1 Chronicles 27:29. He was the father of Shaphat, who had responsibility for the cattle grazing in the valleys during King David's reign. Adlai is known exclusively through his son, who was one of David's trusted officials. Although we know nothing more about Adlai himself, his son's prominent position indicates that the family held a certain status and enjoyed the king's trust.

versions.summary: Adlai is mentioned in 1 Chronicles 27:29 as the father of Shaphat, the overseer who had charge of the herds in the valleys during King David's reign. Although Adlai is mentioned only this once in the Bible, the context provides valuable information. His son held a trusted position in the king's administration, suggesting that the family enjoyed esteem and trust in the united kingdom. Adlai's place in the text illustrates how Chronicles preserves genealogies linked to important administrative roles, even when the person himself plays no independent role in the narrative.

A small clarification might be helpful.; [minor] The value 'shafat' as a child-id is reasonable, but it should be verified that this is consistent with other profiles in the system. footnotes.text: The name Adlai (עַדְלַי) has an uncertain etymology. Some scholars view it as a shortened form of a theophoric name, possibly derived from the root עדל or as a variant of 'Adiel' (עֲדִיאֵל), meaning 'God's ornament'. Others link it to an Aramaic root. The exact meaning remains debated among Hebrew scholars.

1 Chronicles 27:25–31 offers a rare glimpse into the administrative organization under King David. The list of overseers covers everything from grain stores to vineyards and livestock, testifying to a well-developed bureaucracy in the united kingdom. Such lists have parallels in administrative texts from the ancient Near East.

The valleys (Hebrew: עֲמָקִים, amaqim) mentioned in connection with Shaphat's oversight may refer to several fertile lowland areas, including the Shephelah region or other valley districts suitable as grazing lands for cattle in ancient Israel.

The authors of Chronicles placed great emphasis on documenting administrative structures and genealogies. The fact that Adlai is named as the father of one of David's overseers suggests that recording family lines was important for legitimizing positions in the king's service. This reflects a theological concern with order and divine sanctioning of David's kingdom.
